t: Sleep, stress and recovery as determinants of cognitive performance and maintenance in working adults: an evidence-graded narrative review
d: The largest levers are subtractive — protecting sleep, limiting acute stress and exhaustion, and enabling detachment — and their costs are under-felt. This favours objective, baseline-relative measurement over self-report. Trials in working-age professionals are needed.

t: Which popular cognitive-enhancement claims hold up? An evidence-graded narrative review for working adults
d: The additive inputs most heavily marketed for cognition have the weakest or null evidence, while better-supported levers are mostly subtractive or concern deficiency and overall pattern. Detailed meal logging does not meet the evidence bar for cognitive benefit.

t: How knowledge workers work, move and learn: an evidence-graded narrative review of interruptions, breaks, physical activity, learning strategies, social engagement and generative AI
d: The best-supported practices protect attention from fragmentation, use breaks and movement for energy rather than as performance boosters, pair AI use with verification, and build learning on retrieval and spacing. Long-term associations are real but modest and mostly observational. Trials in working-age professionals and founders are needed.
